title: Ferrofluid Speaker
description: The desktop ferrofluid-speaker gadget: a clear vial of black ferrofluid over an electromagnet, seen from the side, with the music driving the field. The flat pool goes unstable and throws up a crown of sharp Rosensweig spikes that climb, lean and dance with the bass, then sink back between beats — shaded like oily black chrome with a wet specular streak, standing in a lit glass cylinder over a glowing coil. Turn on the mic to drive it live; with no mic it runs on a synthetic kick so it always dances. Audio drive, spike height/count, sharpness, sway, viscosity, fluid amount, vessel and sheen hue are live.
